# Decisions: binding-follows-session

- 2026-08-13T16:42:32.967Z — rule: **sofar_end_session binds the current branch to the session's home — MOVING an existing binding only, never creating one, and never onto a closed or dropped record. Resolution itself stays branch-first: never infer a fresh session's record from recency or peer liveness.** — chose **Make the branch binding self-maintaining at write-back time: sofar_end_session, after appending session_ended, binds the current branch to the initiative the write-back landed in. Three guards. It only MOVES a binding that already exists, so a branch deliberately left unbound (sofar new --no-bind) stays unbound. It skips a home whose initiative is closed or dropped. It is best-effort — a detached HEAD, a missing or malformed bindings.json, any throw at all leaves the write-back untouched. The rebind is reported back to the caller as an optional `rebound` field on the result, omitted when nothing moved, following the parallel_writebacks precedent.** over Three alternatives, all rejected. (a) Redirecting a fresh session's RESOLUTION to the most recently active initiative — the user's first framing, and session-orientation D2's rejected option (a). (b) The user's refinement of (a): detect whether parallel sessions are running and prefer the last initiative a session finished in, computed at read time. (c) Binding at RE-HOME time inside sofar_start_session rather than at write-back. Also rejected: leaving it alone and relying on sofar switch, and adding a statusline marker for the mismatch instead of fixing the underlying fact. because The user's instinct — "last initiative a session finished in, discounting live peers" — is right, and this delivers exactly that answer while computing none of it. A live peer has not ended, so it never moves the binding; the branch therefore names the last CONCLUDED work, which is what "open on what I was last working on" means. (b) cannot be built honestly: sibling liveness is not knowable from the record. fold.ts:927 already says so in the codebase's own words, that a sibling with no session_closed "might be a crashed process that would linger as a false conflict forever", and this repo proves it empirically — four sessions are open without write-back right now (6efd8ee9, 2b0bd269, 7e56a4a0, 74e0b536). Resolution built on that signal degrades every time a session crashes. (a) is settled by D2 and nothing here reopens it: resolveBound feeds handlePostTool and every other hook, so redirecting resolution moves where events LAND, and this changes no resolution code at all. Read-time inference also loses on three counts a write-time fact wins: it is invisible, where `cat .sofar/bindings.json` states exactly what the next session gets; it is unoverridable, where `sofar switch` beats a binding permanently; and it costs a per-hook scan of N logs, where session-orientation 2.3 measured 1.7ms for 38 initiatives on the SessionStart path alone and brillo has 59. (c) is refuted by the session that took this decision: it re-homed drift-certification to session-orientation purely to diagnose the report, and a re-home-time rebind would have pointed this repo's main at a CLOSED record. Write-back time also keeps the tree clean — bindings.json is committed, so the rebind lands inside the write-back moment and is committed with the record, obeying the protocol's write-back-then-commit order rather than leaving trailing dirt. Move-only rather than create because an unbound branch is a deliberate state in this repo (session-orientation itself was created with --no-bind so a peer's branch resolution would not move), and a fresh session on an unbound branch already gets a clear "not bound to an initiative" block telling it to switch. Evidence this is worth building: brillo's main stayed bound to baseui-toast-migration across 8 project-tax-architecture commits, so every fresh session there opened on the wrong record and needed the same manual re-home. Known limitation, accepted: with several peers on one branch the last to write back wins, so the binding becomes "most recently finished" rather than "correct". That is strictly better than weeks-stale, it cannot tear a live peer because homeInitiative treats the branch slug only as a seed candidate that any strictly later session_started displaces (mcp/context.ts:194), and session-orientation's notice remains the backstop for exactly that residue. Reverses the property test/rehome.test.ts pins at line 208-211, but narrowly: re-homing still touches nothing, and that test's own case still passes untouched because the peer's home IS the branch's record.
- 2026-08-13T16:58:12.373Z — rule: **Never make the recent-work notice weigh whether a candidate's session is still live. Ending is an event; being alive is not, and the notice names a candidate rather than judging it.** — chose **Drop 3.1. The recent-work notice keeps ranking candidates purely by newest append, with the existing initiative_status_changed suppression as its only type-aware rule. Re-open only on measured noise from a released rebind, not on prediction.** over Having the notice prefer a candidate whose newest event is a session_ended over one mid-flight, so it points at concluded work rather than a peer's live edit — offered to the user this session and declined on inspection. because It gets the important case backwards. After D1's rebind the branch already names the last CONCLUDED work, so the only firing left is a candidate mid-flight — and that population contains both the peer edit this would rightly suppress and the session that re-homed, worked and died without a write-back, which is exactly when the notice earns its keep. This repo carries four such sessions open with no write-back right now. Separating them needs sibling liveness, which is not derivable from the record: the same wall that rejected read-time inference in D1, reappearing inside the one surface deliberately built to NAME a candidate rather than judge it. The existing initiative_status_changed suppression is not a precedent — a status change is unambiguously "not worked", whereas an absent session_ended is ambiguous between finished-badly and still-going. Frequency was the whole motive and the rebind already answers it: the chronic firing in brillo came from a binding stale across 8 commits, not from peers. So the honest order is to release the rebind and measure whether the notice is still noisy, the same order plan-carry-forward used when its Phase 1 measurement did not survive its own premise.
